paper.title: RoCo: Dialectic Multi-Robot Collaboration with Large Language Models
paper.central_claim: RoCo: zero-shot multi-robot collaboration where each robot is an LLM agent in a dialog that ends in a sub-task plan, validated by environment feedback (parse, task constraints, IK, collision, waypoints) and re-discussed until valid, then executed through an RRT multi-arm motion planner informed by LLM-proposed 3D waypoints; it reaches high success rates across all six RoCoBench tasks, adapts to task variations, and supports a human-in-the-loop real-robot collaboration.
paper.claim_type_note: Also introduces RoCoBench and RoCoBench-Text; self-described method contribution comes first (anchors v2 precedent 3).

scope_check.reason: GPT-4 agents with environment validators and a motion planner controlling simulated multi-arm manipulation and a real arm; A class.

signatures.object: Per-robot LLM agents in a round-based dialog that produce a joint sub-task plan, gated by a validation chain before dispatch.
signatures.information: Each agent sees its own task context, capabilities, current observation (asymmetric), round history, communication instruction and optional plan feedback; Central Plan oracle sees everything.
signatures.operation: Discuss until the last speaker proposes a plan -> parse, task-constraint, IK, collision (and waypoint) checks -> on failure append reasons and re-discuss up to K attempts -> else skip the round.
signatures.output: One sub-task (and optional 3D waypoint path) per robot, converted to joint goal configurations.
signatures.conditions: Simulation with oracle object state; 2-3 robots; real world single robot + human with OWL-ViT scene text.
signatures.feedback: Structured validator reasons (IK failure, collision, format) plus next observation.
signatures.selection_rule: First plan passing all validations is executed; at most K re-plans (value not stated).
signatures.persistence: Round history H (dialog + executed actions) within an episode only.
signatures.later_use: Appended to subsequent prompts of the same episode.
signatures.claimed_effect: Success 0.44-0.95 across six tasks vs oracle central planner; removing feedback lowers success on 5/6 tasks.
signatures.failure_boundary: Factual errors propagate between agents; oracle perception; open-loop execution; every dialog turn costs an LLM call.

signatures.object: LLM-proposed 3D task-space waypoint paths used as intermediate goals for a centralized RRT multi-arm planner.
signatures.information: Start/goal/obstacle coordinates in task space given to the LLM; waypoints must be IK-solvable, collision-free and evenly spaced.
signatures.operation: LLM emits waypoints -> validator -> RRT between successive goal configurations.
signatures.conditions: Tasks with high workspace overlap (Pack Grocery, Move Rope).
signatures.claimed_effect: Faster planning for placing; no clear benefit for picking (Fig 4 only).
signatures.failure_boundary: Spatial reasoning degrades with grid size and obstacle count (toy example).

gap.author_gap: Multi-robot systems need task-specific engineering, high-level allocation with capability awareness and joint-space motion planning; prior LLM-robotics work is single-robot/single-thread.
gap.checked_gap: Supported as a gap in published LLM-robotics at the time (single-robot SayCan/Inner Monologue/CaP/TAMP lines). The paper does not test whether dialog is needed: an information-rich centralized LLM planner matches or beats dialog on 4/6 tasks.
lineage: SayCan, Inner Monologue, CaP, TidyBot, Instruct2Act (single robot)

closest_adjacent.name: Inner Monologue (Huang et al. 2022b)
closest_adjacent.solves: environment feedback in-context planning, single robot

gap.residue: Dialog is necessary only when information is asymmetric; coordination quality on tasks with tight workspace overlap; real multi-robot execution not shown.
gap.stakes: Reusable zero-shot coordination across embodiments with interpretable communication.
gap.remaining_gap: Open-loop execution, oracle perception, no real multi-robot results, no dialog-vs-nondialog LLM baseline with matched information.
gap.unresolved: Concurrent LLM multi-agent works not locally pinned; novelty search not performed.

claims.text: RoCo achieves high success rates across all tasks in RoCoBench.
claims.setting: Six MuJoCo tabletop tasks with oracle state; GPT-4.
claims.baseline_control: Central Plan oracle; Dialog w/o history; Dialog w/o feedback.
claims.selection_vs_test: Benchmark built by the authors; no held-out split.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Success >= 0.75 on four of six tasks and 0.44/0.65 on Pack Grocery/Move Rope; comparable to an information-rich oracle on some tasks.

claims.baseline_control: Dialog w/o Feedback with doubled episode budget.
claims.result_denominator: Success equal or higher with feedback on 6/6 tasks, e.g. 0.80 vs 0.35 (Make Sandwich).
claims.allowed_conclusion: Within RoCoBench with oracle validators, the feedback loop is load-bearing.

claims.text: LLM-proposed waypoints speed up multi-arm motion planning.
claims.setting: Pack Grocery and Move Rope snapshots, 300 s budget.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Faster placing plans; no benefit for picking; numbers unavailable in text.

claims.text: RoCo adapts to task variations and works with a human collaborator on a real robot.
claims.setting: Make Sandwich variations (qualitative); real UR5E + human sorting blocks.
claims.selection_vs_test: Real task chosen by the authors.
claims.allowed_conclusion: A single LLM agent can collaborate with a human on one real sorting task at 60-90% over 10 runs per setup; no real multi-robot result.

assessment.evidence_level_reason: Closed-loop simulator success with 20 runs per task plus real-robot counts; real task was authored for this paper, uses a human collaborator and a single robot, and the simulation uses oracle state, so transfer is not granted.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: With oracle simulator state and GPT-4, multi-agent dialog with a validator feedback loop completes four of six authored multi-robot tabletop tasks at >= 0.75 success and the feedback loop is load-bearing; a single-robot-plus-human real demonstration succeeds in 6-9 of 10 runs per setup.
assessment.cannot_claim: High success on all six tasks, necessity of dialog over a centralized planner, real multi-robot collaboration, closed-loop execution robustness, cost viability.
unresolved: Pack Grocery success definition vs reported SE

G.reason: Real, sourced gap against single-robot LLM planners with named neighbors, but nearest concurrent multi-agent LLM work is not compared and dialog necessity versus an information-rich central LLM planner is left unresolved.

M.reason: Dialog + typed plan + geometric validators + RRT is a coherent answer to asymmetric information and motion-planning blowup; the added value of the dialog over a central LLM plan is not established (oracle wins 4/6).

X.reason: Prompt components, protocol, validation order and algorithm are reconstructable; max re-plans, dialog length and round limits are symbols only; oracle perception and open-loop execution bound validity and are disclosed.

measurement.reason: Simulator-judged success with 20 runs per task, steps and re-plans per method, and real-world counts; but oracle state, undefined success judge in the real runs, Pack Grocery SEs inconsistent with binary success over 20 runs, and Fig 4 data in figures only.

causality.reason: Central/oracle, no-history and no-feedback variants with GPT-4 fixed show the feedback loop is load-bearing; confounds remain (no-feedback gets doubled budget, validators not ablated individually, dialog vs central not information-matched, single backbone).

holdout.reason: All six tasks are authored for the method and no development/test separation is stated; only the real-world task and qualitative Make Sandwich variations lie outside; GPT-4 contamination is not addressed.

statistics.reason: Repeated 20-run trials with standard errors for success, but steps/re-plans lack spread, no paired tests, failures only qualitatively analyzed, and one SE pattern is unexplained.

cost.reason: Re-plan attempts and step counts allow a rough LLM-call inference and the waypoint experiment states a 300 s planning budget, but no token/latency/dollar data and the baseline budgets are not matched.

status_reason: Complete body, appendices and PDF supplement read; all eight ratings resolved.
